reviews.comment: The "exams" are just a quick application that you use what you learned from class on gradescope and take no longer than 15-30 minutes to do. Just make sure your group that you partner with for the semester is able to carry their own load of work (even if they dont the work is braindead so you can do it yourself if needed). Would reccomend, ez class

A lot of students are criticizing CSCE121 and not the actual prof. I took him fall 2023 and he was great: explained all content clearly and made sure everyone in the section understood. Very kind and awesome person. Homework will take a while, but not more than other classes by far. Easy tests. Do not be afraid taking this class early due to etam.
Super easy class, just felt like an exhausting amount of busywork. A bit boring, but the class was still informative.

Dr. Moore made HCI a very fun and entertaining course. The concepts were very interesting and I feel like I learned a lot. Assignments were simple and had clear grading criteria and projects were engaging and amusing. He is truly a great professor. I would definitely recommend this class for an upper-level CSCE elective.

This class can be challenging for those who are not cs. Homework is 40% of your grade and is graded solely on completion. The tests are relatively straightforward, with the average score typically ranging between 80 and 85. However, the professor's lectures can be difficult to follow, and I found them to offer little value despite being mandatory.

The homework was so awful. It took roughly 12-14 hours weekly towards the end, and oftentimes, the grading criteria was so convoluted that even TAs and other professors didn't know what we were doing wrong. Awful class, awful professor.

Dr. Moore made accessible computing a fun and interesting class. There was a short assignment each week, in-class activities, simple quizzes on the textbooks, and a group project at the end. The class was fairly simple, yet immersive, insightful, and organized. I truly enjoyed this class and would recommend it to anyone for a CSCE elective.

Dr. Moore actually turned out to be great. He goes into detail during lectures, and is pretty passionate about CS. Dr. Moore also cares about his students, and even had a 1 hour private debugging session with me.

The homework for this class was extremely time consuming, with some taking me over 10 hours. It's critical to start them early.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: John Moore is a nice enough guy, but he's not that great a teacher and nothing you learn in class is really all too useful for the exams. The class is also quite difficult, with homework taking many many hours, but that's not his fault, it's just the nature of the class

Great Prof. I took him in person and he did a wonderful job of explaining all the concepts this year. I don't know why his other scores are so low. This prof is amazing. Yes the HW's are hard, but they are the same hws for everyone in CSCE 120/121. If you are going to take CSCE 120/121 you should definitely take John Michael Moore.

Easy A, but learned almost nothing. So much homework but none of it gets graded until the very end of the semester. Group project does not even have multipliers to show who did all the work. Just do all the assignments and reading and there is no way you won't get an A. Exams are weird, but there are regrades which can fix any problems.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Took the async version of this class with the professor. This class is difficult for an intro to c++ class but makes you learn a lot. HWs are pretty challenging, especially later in the semester.

The best bet at passing this class is resources outside of class. It is a self-taught, self-graded course with little to no interaction from any professor, including your assigned one. I would highly recommend taking this course over the summer or as a transfer since the professors have little to no respect for the students and fail to teach at all
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Haven't really interacted with him. This class is pretty hard ngl. The class is structured relatively well although the zybooks aren't too helpful. They give you a flaky intro and then you have to figure out how to do everything else. The exams were fairly difficult. And the homeworks take forever. Wish y'all the best of luck in this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: CSCE436 is the easiest cs class Ive taken. Weekly assignments are not overly time consuming, tests are easy and open notes (cheat sheet if in person), 2 txtbk readings a week are graded by ai on comments and dont actually need to be read, and the group project expectations are chill. Take this class for an easy and interesting A.

CSCE121 is NOT an intro class to programming, and dont expect easy grading, light homeworks loads or extra credit. He stated very clear in the syllabus, and you can test yourself in the mini quiz before class. Mr John Moore is very knowledgeable when I ask for help. If you want a professor who can push you to limit, take him. You will learn a lot

CSCE 121 is an extremely hard class. Moore doesn't do much to help that. As far as I can tell he is a very nice guy, however he does not know how to teach to the class. Expect to spend hours a week figuring out homework yourself while attending lectures only tangentially related. Not the worst CSCE 121 teacher though, so there is that.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I wish if he actually teaches as a real into level instead of advanced level. The exams are nothing to compare to practice exams he gives us. He's a great guy but I wish he could done a better job as a better prof and understand that most student's don't experience with computer science in C++

Amazing prof for CSCE 121. I took it online; there was a decent amount of homework and labs, but nothing too difficult. If you already have high school programming knowledge then learning C++ won't be bad at all. Be sure to either attend office hours or schedule Zoom meetings with him, he's very good at answering questions.

Moore spends the majority of class trying to prove he can code in C++ rather than helping students understand. Reading zybooks alone is better than listening to lecture in addition. Some common HW assignments are poorly written and it takes time to understand what they want, with the hw's being time-consuming as is. Overall it's poorly structured.

Moore definitely tries to help as best he can, but he tends to just code in class without truly explaining what he is doing. Mimir autograding software is finicky at best and is often extremely frustrating, and profs tend to avoid answering questions. Piazza available and can occasionally be helpful. Overall, it's laughable to call this an intro.

Dr. Moore's class was great! He was so helpful, and always willing to help me in his office with debugging code. 121 isn't supposed to be your first programming class, it's best to have prior knowledge of coding, but doesn't have to be C++. The class can be challenging, but he teaches it well. Be ready to work and get help. Dr. Moore is great

If you don't have extensive knowledge of c++ beforehand, avoid Moore. The fact that this is an intro to CSCE class is laughable. Not to mention, the auto-grading mimir software is frustrating and unhelpful.
Just expects you to know all the stuff beforehand.

Everyone hates Moore, but he's really a good guy. His first test is the hardest, but after that, you should be fine. If you don't have coding knowledge, don't take him maybe start in the other intro class. Lectures are boring, but you get credit for just showing up. The TAs take FOREVER to grade. That's the only thing that's annoyed me
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really nice guy. Lectures aren't very helpful, but are relevant if you pay attention. His review sessions are just Q&A, but if you ask, he will go through most of the material. The exams and homework are relatively easy, but the material gets pretty difficult near the end. Overall, a solid choice.

AVOID MOORE AT ALL COSTS. Teaching is derived mostly from online and paper textbooks. Homework, test review sheets, etc. are very vague. Attendance is mandatory yet lectures are useless. He was no help during office hours. This is supposed to be an intro course to C++ yet he expects knowledge of C++ and exams don't focus on the programming aspects

This prof is absolutely horrible. To save the quality of your life, avoid him at every cost. Hes lectures are mandatory for attendance or he will fail you but the lectures are absolute garbage as he just types code all class without any class participation. The class is supposed to be intro level but he likes to flex his PhD to freshman students...
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The title of my class with him is "Intro to Programming Design and Concepts" and one of the very first things he said was "I expect you to have some background in some sort of programming." What? He didn't actually teach us much, he relied mostly on the zybooks. Tried emailing him outside of class and he didn't respond because it wasn't piazza. Ugh

Really nice guy, cares for his students. Pretty scatterbrained, and his lectures can be really boring, so most people didn't attend class. Tests were only 10-20% each with the rest being homework. I appreciated the split because you could get a good grade if you just spent enough time on the homework and got 100s on all the assignments.

Assigns quite a bit of busy work as his "curve" to the class. Extremely unorganized. Homework assignments are overly complicated and it's not because of the topics. His instructions don't make sense and constantly contradict one another. Don't bother going to him for help, he'll spend the whole time distracted on his computer. TA's were helpful.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Avoid this prof if possible. The homework is extremely tedious and is much more intense than it should be for an introductory-level course. Instructions are extremely unclear, and sometimes change from when the assignment is given to when you turn it in. Also, I learn nothing from lecture, only from the online textbook, but attendance is mandatory.

Moore is a very cool guy, but not a good professor. The homework was incredibly difficult and very vague, we did not have grades back in a timely manner and he made this class way more difficult than it needed to be. I've been programming for years and I absolutely hated this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK
